speaker: (the curate)
text: The sand is out, and I have a little yet to say.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Sit, Will. The bench is under thee.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Sitting is worse. I'll stand the rest of it.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: Then stand, son. Don't make a second sermon of a back.

speaker: (the curate)
text: A man goes out. A man, if he is suffered, comes again.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: He means the road.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: He means the epistle. The road is mine. I brought it in with me.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Thou hast been on it since Thursday, and thou art not out of the house.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: An hour on your feet will not start a horse, and it will not mend what the barn took.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The horse is tomorrow, and it is not mine. Today I can stand.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: The road is tomorrow. You were still on it in the lane, before the bell.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then you are ahead of the sermon. The glass is done. So am I.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: The glass is done when he says it is done. Thou art not the clerk of it.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: He has said it. The sand is out. Grandmother already has the pie in her head.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: The pie is cold, and it is at home, and standing here will not warm it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not standing to warm a pie. I am standing because the bench is worse.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Then we have heard it. The hour is stood. Do not give it an epilogue in the aisle.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: People are looking. Come down the nave like a man who has been to church, not like a man who has won it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have not won it. I have lasted it. There is a difference, and I am taking it home.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: Home is the difference. The barn is not in this church, and I will not have it preached a second time between here and the door.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Thou stood the whole of the hour. Don't look as if it were a part.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: Home. There is a cold pie, and it will not wait on a back.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: I'll walk with you. The lane is short, and you can be ordinary in it.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Ordinary will do. We have had the hour. We do not need a second one between the door and the house.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I'm coming. I'll come standing.
